name: DAVERAGE

args.name: database
args.about: the table, with its header row

args.name: field
args.about: the column to average: its header in quotes, or its number

args.name: criteria
args.about: a range with a header and the conditions below it

about: Gives the average of a column, over the rows of a table that match the criteria.

example.why: The criteria A7:A8 pick the rows whose Team is Sales: (3200 + 3500) / 2 = 3350.

notes: AVERAGEIFS does the same without a criteria block.

name: DCOUNT

args.name: database
args.about: the table, with its header row

args.name: field
args.about: the column to count numbers in (left out to count matching rows): its header in quotes, or its number

args.name: criteria
args.about: a range with a header and the conditions below it

about: Counts the numbers in a column, over the rows of a table that match the criteria.

example.why: The criteria A7:A8 pick the rows whose Team is Sales: Ann and Cat, both with a number in Pay.

notes: DCOUNTA counts any non-empty cell, not only numbers.

name: DGET

args.name: database
args.about: the table, with its header row

args.name: field
args.about: the column to read: its header in quotes, or its number

args.name: criteria
args.about: a range with a header and the conditions below it

about: Gives the one value in a column from the row of a table that matches the criteria.

example.why: The criteria B7:B8 pick the row whose Name is Bob, and his Pay is 2800.

notes: If more than one row matches it gives #NUM!; if none, #VALUE!.

name: DMAX

args.about: the table, with its header row

args.name: field
args.about: the column to look at: its header in quotes, or its number

args.name: criteria
args.about: a range with a header and the conditions below it

about: Gives the biggest number in a column, over the rows of a table that match the criteria.

example.why: The criteria A7:A8 pick the rows whose Team is Sales; the bigger of 3200 and 3500 is 3500.

notes: MAXIFS does the same without a criteria block.

name: DPRODUCT

args.name: database
args.about: the table, with its header row

args.name: field

args.name: criteria
args.about: a range with a header and the conditions below it

name: DSTDEV

args.name: database
args.about: the table, with its header row

args.name: field
args.about: the column to look at: its header in quotes, or its number

args.name: criteria
args.about: a range with a header and the conditions below it

about: Gives the standard deviation of a column, over the rows of a table that match the criteria, treating them as a sample.

example.why: The criteria A7:A8 pick the rows whose Team is Sales: the pays 3200 and 3500 give a sample variance of 45000, whose square root is about 212.13.

notes: DSTDEVP treats the rows as the whole population.

name: DVAR

args.name: database
args.about: the table, with its header row

args.name: field
args.about: the column to look at: its header in quotes, or its number

args.name: criteria
args.about: a range with a header and the conditions below it

about: Gives the variance of a column, over the rows of a table that match the criteria, treating them as a sample.

example.why: The criteria A7:A8 pick the rows whose Team is Sales: the pays 3200 and 3500 are 150 either side of 3350, so (150² + 150²) / (2 − 1) = 45000.

notes: DVARP treats the rows as the whole population.

name: DVARP

args.name: database
args.about: the table, with its header row

args.name: field
args.about: the column to look at: its header in quotes, or its number

args.name: criteria
args.about: a range with a header and the conditions below it

about: Gives the variance of a column, over the rows of a table that match the criteria, treating them as the whole population.

example.why: The criteria A7:A8 pick the rows whose Team is Sales: the pays are 150 either side of 3350, so (150² + 150²) / 2 = 22500.

notes: DVAR treats the rows as a sample.

name: DSTDEVP

args.name: database
args.about: the table, with its header row

args.name: field
args.about: the column to look at: its header in quotes, or its number

args.name: criteria
args.about: a range with a header and the conditions below it

about: Gives the standard deviation of a column, over the rows of a table that match the criteria, treating them as the whole population.

example.why: The criteria A7:A8 pick the rows whose Team is Sales: the pays are 150 either side of their average, so the deviation is 150.

notes: DSTDEV treats the rows as a sample.
